messages.subject: Overlay grid on world map
parts:
I have a dataframe with x,y coordinates. I've sampled some x,y coordinates from my dataframe:

y <-c(24.637032,21.569813,21.687,19.677183,24.72438,21.433136)

x <-c(-156.02597,-112.00287,-112.00287,-105.27803,-159.47324,-157.858)

I've converted these points to a SpatialPoints objects:

library(sp)
myPoints <- data.frame(x,y)
coordinates(myPoints) <- c('x', 'y')
proj4string(myPoints) <- CRS("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84")

I've used these points to make a SpatialGridobject:

bb <- bbox(myPoints)
cs <- c(1, 1)
myPointsGrid <- GridTopology(cellcentre.offset =  bb[, 1] + (cs/2), cellsize = cs, cells.dim = ceiling(diff(t(bb))/cs))
myPointsGrid <- SpatialGrid(myPointsGrid, proj4string = "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84")

I need two things 1.overlay myPointsGrid on a world map (I believe geom_tile can do this) 2. plot myPoints on world map

The base layer for my world map is:

world <- map_data('world') 
ggplot(aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group),  data=world, colour="black", fill="white", alpha=0) + geom_polygon()

Hi Ross,

You seem to know how to proceed, so I'm not sure why you haven't. See
in line for more.

On Fri, Feb 15, 2013 at 7:31 AM, Ross <ross...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> I have a dataframe with x,y coordinates. I've sampled some x,y coordinates
> from my dataframe:
>
> y <-c(24.637032,21.569813,21.687,19.677183,24.72438,21.433136)
>
> x <-c(-156.02597,-112.00287,-112.00287,-105.27803,-159.47324,-157.858)
>
> I've converted these points to a SpatialPoints objects:
>
> library(sp)
> myPoints <- data.frame(x,y)
> coordinates(myPoints) <- c('x', 'y')
> proj4string(myPoints) <- CRS("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84")
>
> I've used these points to make a SpatialGridobject:
>
> bb <- bbox(myPoints)
> cs <- c(1, 1)
> myPointsGrid <- GridTopology(cellcentre.offset = bb[, 1] + (cs/2), cellsize
> = cs, cells.dim = ceiling(diff(t(bb))/cs))
> myPointsGrid <- SpatialGrid(myPointsGrid, proj4string = "+proj=longlat
> +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84")
>
> I need two things 1.overlay myPointsGrid on a world map (I believe geom_tile
> can do this)
Right, so why not give it a try? Here is what I did:

ggplot(aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group),
data=world,
colour="black",
fill="white", alpha=0) +

geom_polygon() +
geom_tile(aes(x=x, y=y, group=NULL),
fill=alpha("white", 0), data=as.data.frame(myPointsGrid),
color="red")
Surely you know how to plot points:

ggplot(aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group),
data=world,
colour="black",
fill="white", alpha=0) +

geom_polygon() +
geom_tile(aes(x=x, y=y, group=NULL),
fill=alpha("white", 0), data=as.data.frame(myPointsGrid),
color="red") +
geom_point(aes(x=x, y=y, group=NULL),
data=as.data.frame(myPoints),
color="blue")

I hope this didn't come off as rude, I'm not trying to be--just
genuinely puzzled since you seemed to know the answers already.

Best,
Ista
